name: Custom Zango app
one_liner: Any business app on plain Zango: describe its roles, data, workflows and pages in one spec and watch a clickable preview of it take shape before anything is built.
fits_when: no domain template fits the requirement
the app is mostly records, forms, lists and approval workflows
different roles see different menus, records and actions
a record moves through statuses with role-gated transitions
a central record needs a 360 page with related lists and a timeline
gives_you: Roles with their own menus and landing pages
List pages with search, filters, quick views and row actions
Create and edit forms with validation and duplicate checks
Status workflows with role-gated transitions, tags and confirmations
Row-level access per role, including external logins that see only their own records
360 pages with header facts, stats, related tabs and an activity timeline

catalogue.description: A generic Zango app described in the Zango app spec (v1): roles and menus, modules and entities with fields, access, workflows, forms and list tables, and 360 detail pages. The spec is previewed live as a clickable app with demo data while the requirement is shaped.

changelog: 1.1.41: the default model for AI helpers on Anthropic is claude-sonnet-5-5. 1.1.40: AI helpers can sit anywhere: `where: row | list | form` on button and chat triggers (row menus, list headers, inside forms) and `type: ai` 360 tabs, summary sections and sidebar panels showing a helper's answer with Run; the preview simulates each. 1.1.39: `ai` section: AI helpers (Zango AI agents) with what they read, what they produce and where it goes, who checks it, and when they run (record events, schedule, button, fill-from-document, chat, or from code via a custom requirement's `uses_ai`); the checker validates them and spec_mark_ready needs each helper's acceptance and preview.sample. 1.1.38: the Back button on a record's not-found box is chrome. 1.1.37: generated record pages and Overview tabs are not marked as YAML paths (they have none). 1.1.36: every record opens full page: an entity with no detail view gets a generated one (<entity>_record), every detail view opens on Overview (all fields), rows in any table open their record and Back returns to where they came from; the current stepper step has a green tick. 1.1.35: the 360 stepper sits under the header without a divider. 1.1.34: the name under a code-first 360 title is not a heading (the prototype check reads it as the title). 1.1.33: a record code leading a 360 subtitle heads the title line in mono, the title under it. 1.1.32: 360 header facts sit under the title as one meta line (values split by dots, the label as a tooltip); sidebar panels draw as a compact summary card (label left, value right). Lists and 360s draw more of a designed app, in the preview as the built app does: crud pages take `stats` (KPI tiles between the header and the table, a count or a sum over the rows the viewer sees); columns take `badge` (a pill after the value when `when` holds) and, on a status column, `progress` (a step bar and "Step i of n"); `table.row_chevron` adds a chevron at the end of clickable rows; `detail_views[].header.stepper` draws the hero's lifecycle with an end marker for a status off the steps; a menu item takes `count` (true or {where}); `app.shell.user: top` puts the user card above the menu.
